title: Microalgal Colony Blot for Direct Detection of Recombinant Proteins
author: Yasin Torres-Tiji

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Materials
steps.instruction: Clean the necessary tools and the work area to ensure sterility.

substeps.instruction: Wipe a ruler, pencil, scissors, and an empty petri dish with 70% ethanol.
Place these items inside a clean biological safety cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare Nitrocellulose Membrane
steps.instruction: Cut and mark the nitrocellulose membrane to fit the petri dish.

substeps.instruction: Use an empty petri dish as a guideline to draw a circle (or other shape) on the membrane with a pencil.
Cut the membrane 1 or 2 mm inside the drawn line to ensure it fits inside the dish.
Draw a grid on the membrane with a pencil (e.g., a 12 by 10 grid consisting of a 6 cm by 5 cm rectangle with 0.5 cm squares), taking care not to break the membrane.

steps.title: Set Up Membrane on Agar
steps.instruction: Transfer the membrane to an agar plate containing the same antibiotic selection used for the transgenic colonies.

substeps.instruction: Place the membrane slowly onto the agar, allowing one side to touch first.
Allow moisture to move onto the membrane via capillarity, ensuring no bubbles are trapped between the membrane and the agar.

steps.title: Spot Algal Biomass onto Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer algal biomass from grown patched plates onto the membrane grid, including a negative control in triplicate (a strain with the same antibiotic selection but not expressing the recombinant protein).

substeps.instruction: Set a P200 pipette to 200 µl.
Press the pipette tip against the algal biomass to collect an equivalent of 1 µl (do not pipette conventionally due to viscosity).
Gently touch the tip to the nitrocellulose membrane surface without puncturing it.
Push the plunger while lifting the pipette to deposit a cylinder or blob of biomass.

steps.title: Incubate Algal Colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate upside down in a growth room at 25-30°C with continuous lighting.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 48 hours for strong protein expression detection, or up to 144 hours or more to increase sensitivity.

steps.title: Remove Cell Debris
steps.instruction: Wash off cell lumps and debris from the membrane surface using TBST and a soft plastic pasteur pipette.

substeps.instruction: Vigorously pipette TBST right next to the colonies to wash off debris.
Gently scratch off remaining algal remains with the pipette tip, avoiding over-scratching to prevent visible marks in the final assay.

steps.title: Block the Membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in a Western Blot blocking solution for 1 hour on a rocking shaker at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Use a proven solution such as Haycock Solution or TBST with 5% non-fat milk powder.

steps.title: Apply Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody according to the manufacturer's instructions.

substeps.instruction: For anti-GFP AP, use a 1:3000 dilution and incubate for 1 hour on a rocking shaker at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash Membrane
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane three times for 10 minutes each with TBST on a rocking shaker at room temperature.

steps.title: Develop the Immunoblot
steps.instruction: Develop the blot using NBT/BCIP substrate solution.

substeps.instruction: Add enough NBT/BCIP substrate solution to cover the membrane (e.g., 2 mL).
Incubate on a rocking shaker at room temperature.
Monitor results: continually for the first 5 minutes, every 2 minutes for the next 10 minutes, and then every 10 minutes for the remainder of the hour (total time up to 1 hour).
Take pictures when results are clearly visible, avoiding saturation.
